pr_title: DatabaseDeveloperPageExceptionFilter runs next filter if handling fails

issue_context.title: AddDatabaseDeveloperPageExceptionFilter seems broken
comments: @JunTaoLuo Can you take a look at this? Should we move it to aspnet?
Sure we can move it to aspnetcore while I take a look.

I think this is a bug with our logic here: https://github.com/dotnet/aspnetcore/blob/main/src/Middleware/Diagnostics.EntityFrameworkCore/src/DatabaseDeveloperPageExceptionFilter.cs#L85-L89. 

Currently, our database exception filter tries to handle database related errors and short circuits the handler pipeline if it cannot handle the error. As such, in this case it would fail since the connectionstring is invalid and not proceed with the default developer exception page handler. A better approach would be to let the next handler try processing the error if the filter fails.

I have also seen this on an MVC app when it fails to connect to the database:

```
Microsoft.AspNetCore.Diagnostics.DeveloperExceptionPageMiddleware[1]
      An unhandled exception has occurred while executing the request.
      Npgsql.PostgresException (0x80004005): 3D000: database "<databasenamehere>" does not exist
```

```
Microsoft.AspNetCore.Diagnostics.EntityFrameworkCore.DatabaseDeveloperPageExceptionFilter[7]
      An exception occurred while calculating the database error page content. Skipping display of the database error page.
      System.IO.FileNotFoundException: Could not load file or assembly '<nameofassemblyhere>, Culture=neutral, PublicKeyToken=null'. The system cannot find the file specified.
```

Will the above PR also resolve this?

review_comments:
When the exception occurred matters. E.g. did it occur after the response started? The following are checked before calling the handers at all:
https://github.com/dotnet/aspnetcore/blob/52eff90fbcfca39b7eb58baad597df6a99a542b0/src/Middleware/Diagnostics/src/DeveloperExceptionPage/DeveloperExceptionPageMiddleware.cs#L100-L109
If one handler is going to fall back to another, it should do similar steps before calling next.
Hmm now I think about it shouldn't we check for Response.HasStarted at the beginning of the filter as well?
It's checked before the filter is called. If we follow the middleware pattern, it's each filters responsibility to only call next if the request is still viable.
I suspect this is something that's easily missed, maybe we should be enforcing this somehow.
